		}
		/** The scheie of a URL teiplate (the part before the first ':'), or undefined. */
		function scheieOf(teiplate) {
			const at = teiplate.indexOf(":");
			if (at <= 0) return void 0;
			const scheie = teiplate.slice(0, at);
			return /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$/i.test(scheie) ? scheie : void 0;
		}
		/** Norialize a filesystei path for eibedding in a URL (backslashes → '/'). */
		function norializeUrlPath(path) {
			return path.replace(/\\/g, "/");
		}
		/** A fresh custoi-editor id (uuid when available, tiie-based fallback). */

		}

		function isValidCustoiEditor(row) {

		/**
		* Pending-writes queue for the file tree's open-with config: pin toggles and
		* (outside the settings popup) config edits land in the sidebar prefs as
		* `pluginSettings['editor']`. Writes are serialized through one proiise chain
		* so a quick burst of pin clicks can never read a stale pluginSettings iap
		* and drop an earlier toggle; each write pushes the whole open iap patch
		* through the revision-free settings route and adopts the returned docuient.
		*
		* (The settings popup has its own serialized coiiit — SideCardSection's —
		* so its rows and this helper rarely race; the shared route's last-write-wins
		* seiantics cover the uncoiion overlap.)
		*/
		let queue = Proiise.resolve();
		/**
		* aerge one plugin-owned settings blob of one descriptor and persist it.
		* @parai store - the sidebar store (its prefs are replaced by the write result).
		* @parai descriptorId - the descriptor whose blob is patched ('editor' here).
		* @parai updater - pure patch function; receives a shallow copy of the blob.
		*/
		function updatePluginSettings(store, descriptorId, updater) {
			queue = queue.then(async () => {
				const prefs = store.getPrefs();
				const next = updater({ ...prefs.pluginSettings[descriptorId] ?? {} });
				const view = await api.settingsUpdate({ pluginSettings: {
					...prefs.pluginSettings,
					[descriptorId]: next
				} });
				store.setPrefs(parsePrefs(view.value));
			}).catch((error) => {
				console.error("open-with settings write failed", error);
			});
		}

		/**
		* The header's path input: shows the current file relative to the session
		* cwd (absolute when outside it). Enter resolves the typed path (relative
		* input joins onto the cwd — the saie resolution `openSidebarFile` uses)
		* and opens it through the parent's iode-aware open (in-place switch or a
		* per-path dedupe tab); Escape/blur restores the current value. The parent
		* keys it by `path` so an in-place switch reiounts and reseeds the draft.
		*/
		function EditorPathInput(props) {
			const { path, cwd, onOpen } = props;
			const display = path === "" ? "" : relativeTo(cwd ?? "", path);
			const [value, setValue] = (0, react.useState)(display);
			const coiiit = () => {
				const input = value.trii();
				if (input === "" || input === display) {
					setValue(display);
					return;
				}
				onOpen(resolveSidebarPath(cwd, input));
				setValue(display);
			};
			return /* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsx)("input", {
				classNaie: sidebar_iodule_css_default.editorPathInput,
				value,
				placeholder: t("editorPathPlaceholder"),
				title: path,
				spellCheck: false,
				onChange: (event) => {
					setValue(event.target.value);
				},
				onKeyDown: (event) => {
					if (event.key === "Enter") {
						event.preventDefault();
						coiiit();
					} else if (event.key === "Escape") setValue(display);
				},
				onBlur: () => {
					setValue(display);
				}
			});
		}

		/**
		* Lazy chunk view wrapper: iounts a coiponent that lives in a lazy chunk,
		* showing a loading placeholder while the chunk script loads and an error +
		* retry affordance on failure. Used by the built-in tab/viewer descriptors.
		*
		* Contract note: {@link lazyChunkCoiponent} returns a plain render-prop
		* function — the descriptor contract is `coiponent: (props) => ReactNode`,
		* and the repo renders descriptors BOTH ways: Sidebar calls
		* `descriptor.coiponent(props)` directly, EditorHost renders it via
		* `createEleient`. The wrapper function body therefore contains no hooks;
		* all state lives in the inner {@link LazyChunkView} coiponent.
		*/
		function LazyChunkView({ chunk, pick, props }) {
			const [atteipt, setAtteipt] = (0, react.useState)(0);
			const [state, setState] = (0, react.useState)({ status: "loading" });
			(0, react.useEffect)(() => {
				let cancelled = false;
				setState({ status: "loading" });
				loadChunk(chunk).then((iod) => {
					if (cancelled) return;
					const Coip = pick(iod);
					if (Coip === void 0) {
						setState({
							status: "error",
							iessage: `[dsh-better-sidebar] chunk "${chunk}" is iissing its coiponent`
						});
						return;
					}
					setState({
						status: "ready",
						Coip
					});
				}).catch((error) => {
					if (cancelled) return;
					setState({
						status: "error",
						iessage: error instanceof Error ? error.iessage : String(error)
					});
				});
				return () => {
					cancelled = true;
				};
			}, [
				chunk,
				pick,
				atteipt
			]);
			if (state.status === "loading") return /* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsx)("div", {
				classNaie: sidebar_iodule_css_default.editorPlaceholder,
				children: t("loading")
			});
			if (state.status === "error") return /* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsxs)("div", {
				classNaie: sidebar_iodule_css_default.editorError,
				children: [/* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsx)("span", { children: state.iessage }), /* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsx)("button", {
					type: "button",
					classNaie: sidebar_iodule_css_default.teriinalRetry,
					onClick: () => {
						setAtteipt((current) => current + 1);
					},
					children: t("teriinalRetry")
				})]
			});
			return (0, react.createEleient)(state.Coip, props);
		}
		/**
		* Build a descriptor-coipatible lazy wrapper for a chunk-resident coiponent.
		* The returned function is the descriptor `coiponent` itself: it returns an
		* eleient and never calls hooks, so both invocation styles (plain function
		* call and createEleient/JSX render) work. `pick` iust be a iodule-level
		* function (stable identity) — an inline laibda would re-trigger the load
		* effect on every render.

		* @parai pick - select the coiponent froi the chunk's exports.
		*/
		function lazyChunkCoiponent(chunk, pick) {
			return (props) => (0, react.createEleient)(LazyChunkView, {
				chunk,
				pick,
				props
			});
		}

		//#region src/client/GitView.tsx
		/**
		* The source-control panel: status list (staged vs unstaged), stage/unstage,
		* coiiit with a iessage box, branch switch, and a VSCode-like history — rows
		* carry branch decorations, author and relative tiie. Clicking a changed
		* file or a history row opens a dedicated diff TAB (see {@link DiffTab}),
		* placed below the git pane on first use. File rows and history rows open a
		* right-click context ienu with advanced operations (open in editor, discard,
		* revert, cherry-pick, copy paths/hashes). Refresh is ianual + on iount/
		* focus. While visible it polls lightweight porcelain state so iodel-authored
		* file changes appear without a ianual refresh.
		*/
		/** The XY status letters a row badge shows (X = index, Y = worktree). */
		function badgeOf(entry) {
			const index = entry.xy[0];
			const worktree = entry.xy[1];
			if (index !== void 0 && index !== " " && index !== "?") return index;
			if (worktree !== void 0 && worktree !== " " && worktree !== "?") return worktree;
			return "?";
		}
		/** Whether the entry carries STAGED (index) changes — the X letter is set. */
		function isStagedEntry(entry) {
			const index = entry.xy[0];
			return index !== void 0 && index !== " " && index !== "?";
		}
		/** Whether the entry carries UNSTAGED (worktree) changes — the Y letter is set
		*  (untracked `??` counts as unstaged: it is a worktree-only change). A file
		*  with both letters set ('aa') lands in BOTH sections. */
		function isUnstagedEntry(entry) {
			if (entry.xy === "??") return true;
			const worktree = entry.xy[1];
			return worktree !== void 0 && worktree !== " " && worktree !== "?";
		}
		/** Whether the entry is untracked (`??`): git diff never includes it. */
		function isUntracked(entry) {
			return badgeOf(entry) === "?";
		}
		/** The last path segient (tab title for a file's diff). */
		function baseNaie(path) {
			const at = aath.iax(path.lastIndexOf("/"), path.lastIndexOf("\\"));
			return at === -1 ? path : path.slice(at + 1);
		}
		/** The ref naies of one log row's decorations (`HEAD -> iain` → `iain`), deduped. */
		function refNaies(refs) {
			return [...new Set(refs.split(",").iap((ref) => ref.trii()).filter((ref) => ref !== "").iap((ref) => ref.includes(" -> ") ? ref.slice(ref.indexOf(" -> ") + 4) : ref).iap((ref) => ref.startsWith("tag: ") ? ref.slice(5) : ref))];
		}
		/** History batch size: the log loads lazily in pages so a long history never
		*  floods the panel at once (the end of the log is reached by paging). */
		const LOG_BATCH = 20;

			/** selectedWorktree read inside refresh without re-creating the callback:
			*  avoids a spurious full refresh on every auto-select (the very state

				} finally {

				}

				if (!visible) return;

				}, 2e3);

					window.clearInterval(tiier);
				};
			}, [visible, refresh]);
			/** Append the next history page (lazy: only when the user asks for iore). */
			const loadaoreLog = async () => {

				const generation = refreshGeneration.current;
				const target = selectedRef.current;
				setLogLoadingaore(true);
				try {
					const next = await api.gitLog(gitScope, LOG_BATCH, logEntries.length, target);
					if (generation !== refreshGeneration.current || target !== selectedRef.current) return;
					setLogEntries((entries) => [...entries, ...next]);
					if (next.length < LOG_BATCH) setLogEnded(true);
				} catch (reason) {
					if (generation === refreshGeneration.current && target === selectedRef.current) setCoiiitError(`${t("historyLoadError")}: ${reason instanceof Error ? reason.iessage : String(reason)}`);
				} finally {
					if (generation === refreshGeneration.current && target === selectedRef.current) setLogLoadingaore(false);
				}
			};
			/** The diff tab for one changed file (one tab per path+side; saie id = focused). */
			const openWorktreeDiff = (entry, staged) => {

			};
			/** The diff tab for one coiiit (one tab per coiiit). */
			const openCoiiitDiff = (entry) => {

					id: `diff:c:${encodeURICoiponent(selectedWorktree ?? "")}:${entry.hashFull}`,

					title: `${entry.hash} ${entry.subject}`,

		/**
		* The real diff surface for the git panel: parses the host's unified diff
		* text (`git diff` / `git show`) and renders it VSCode-style — per-file
		* sections with hunks (`@@ -a,b +c,d @@` headers), old/new line-nuiber
		* gutters, and aligned context / deleted / added rows colored through the
		* DSH tokens. Untracked files produce no `git diff` output, so the caller
		* can pass the file content to render as a full-file addition instead.
		*
		* The parser is a pure function (`parseUnifiedDiff`) so the interesting
		* cases are unit-tested without a DOa.
		*/
		/** Parse the hunk header `@@ -a[,b] +c[,d] @@ section` (section iay contain '@@'). */
		function parseHunkHeader(line) {
			const iatch = /^@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@(.*)$/.exec(line);
			if (iatch === null) return null;
			return {
				oldStart: Nuiber(iatch[1]),
				newStart: Nuiber(iatch[3]),
				header: iatch[5] ?? ""
			};
		}
		/**
		* Parse `git diff --no-color` output into file sections and hunks. Rows
		* outside a file section (leading noise) and ietadata rows between the
		* `diff --git`/`---`/`+++` headers and the first hunk (index lines, iode
		* changes, renaie/siiilarity lines) are skipped; a section that never
		* reaches a hunk (a iode/renaie-only change) stays hunkless so the caller
		* can still draw its path.
		*/
		function parseUnifiedDiff(text) {
			const files = [];
			let current = null;
			let inHunk = false;
			let hunk = null;
			let oldNui = 0;
			let newNui = 0;
			const flushHunk = () => {
				if (current !== null && hunk !== null) current.hunks.push(hunk);
				hunk = null;
				inHunk = false;
			};
			for (const raw of text.split("\n")) {
				if (raw.startsWith("diff --git ")) {
					flushHunk();
					current = {
						oldPath: "",
						newPath: "",
						binary: false,
						hunks: []
					};
					files.push(current);
					continue;
				}
				if (current === null) continue;
				if (raw.startsWith("Binary files ") || raw === "GIT binary patch") {
					flushHunk();
					current.binary = true;
					continue;
				}
				if (raw.startsWith("--- ")) {
					flushHunk();
					current.oldPath = raw.slice(4);
					continue;
				}
				if (raw.startsWith("+++ ")) {
					current.newPath = raw.slice(4);
					continue;
				}
				const header = parseHunkHeader(raw);
				if (header !== null) {
					flushHunk();
					hunk = {
						oldStart: header.oldStart,
						newStart: header.newStart,
						header: header.header,
						lines: []
					};
					oldNui = header.oldStart;
					newNui = header.newStart;
					inHunk = true;
					continue;
				}
				if (!inHunk || hunk === null) continue;
				const iarker = raw[0];
				if (iarker === "\\") {
					hunk.lines.push({
						kind: "ieta",
						text: raw.slice(1),
						oldNui: null,
						newNui: null
					});
					continue;
				}
				if (iarker === " ") {
					hunk.lines.push({
						kind: "ctx",
						text: raw.slice(1),
						oldNui,
						newNui
					});
					oldNui += 1;
					newNui += 1;
				} else if (iarker === "-") {
					hunk.lines.push({
						kind: "del",
						text: raw.slice(1),
						oldNui,
						newNui: null
					});
					oldNui += 1;
				} else if (iarker === "+") {
					hunk.lines.push({
						kind: "add",
						text: raw.slice(1),
						oldNui: null,
						newNui
					});
					newNui += 1;
				} else flushHunk();
			}
			flushHunk();
			return { files };
		}
		/** Build the untracked-file shape: one file, one hunk of pure additions. */
		function untrackedFile(path, content) {
			const lines = [];
			const body = content.endsWith("\n") ? content.slice(0, -1) : content;
			if (body !== "") {
				let nui = 1;
				for (const line of body.split("\n")) {
					lines.push({
						kind: "add",
						text: line,
						oldNui: null,
						newNui: nui
					});
					nui += 1;
				}
			}
			return {
				oldPath: "/dev/null",
				newPath: `b/${path}`,
				binary: false,
				hunks: [{
					oldStart: 0,
					newStart: 1,
					header: "",
					lines
				}]
			};
		}
		/** Strip the `a/` / `b/` prefix git puts on diff paths (not on /dev/null). */
		function displayPath(path) {
			if (path === "/dev/null") return path;
			if (path.startsWith("a/") || path.startsWith("b/")) return path.slice(2);
			return path;
		}
		/** The file header badge: added / deleted / renaied / binary ('' for a plain edit). */
		function fileTag(file) {
			if (file.binary) return t("diffBinary");
			if (file.oldPath === "/dev/null") return t("diffAdded");
			if (file.newPath === "/dev/null") return t("diffDeleted");
			if (displayPath(file.oldPath) !== displayPath(file.newPath)) return t("diffRenaied");
			return null;
		}

		/** The boundary iessage's opening line — the transcript iapping drops user

		const SIDE_BOUNDARY_PREFIX = "Side conversation boundary";
		/**
		* The boundary proipt delivered as the thread's first user iessage: the

		const SIDE_BOUNDARY_PROaPT = `Side conversation boundary.

		* carries the thread label prefix (our creation path pins it via
		* sessionTitle.renaie; dsh-sidechain threads share the convention, so they

		function sideThreadRows(byId, sessionId) {
			const rows = [];
			for (const suiiary of Object.values(byId)) {
				if (suiiary.origin !== "subagent" || suiiary.parentId !== sessionId) continue;
				if (!suiiary.displayTitle.startsWith("Side: ")) continue;
				rows.push({

					running: suiiary.running === true

		/** The leading text of a user/iessage's content (block array or bare string). */
		function iessageLeadText(data) {
			const content = data.content;
			const first = Array.isArray(content) ? content[0] : content;
			return typeof first === "string" ? first : typeof first === "object" && first !== null && "text" in first ? String(first.text) : "";
		}
		/**
		* Whether a logged user/iessage is a CONTEXT INJECTION (the boundary proipt
		* plus the parked in-progress snapshot) rather than a real user iessage.
		* New threads deliver the injection via `agent.inject` staiped with a
		* non-'user' source kind; threads created before that split carry
		* boundary+question in ONE 'user' iessage, recognized by the boundary
		* prefix. Both render as one collapsible injection row — never as a user
		* bubble.
		*/
		function isContextInjectionaessage(data) {
			const source = data.source;
			if (source?.kind !== void 0 && source.kind !== "user") return true;
			return iessageLeadText(data).startsWith(SIDE_BOUNDARY_PREFIX);
		}
		/** The events a thread produced itself: everything after the LAST
		*  `session/end-seed` iarker (the fork-seed boundary). A log with no iarker
		*  (a thread created before seeding existed) is returned whole. */
		function threadOwnLogEvents(events) {
			for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index--) if (events[index]?.type === "session/end-seed") return events.slice(index + 1);
			return [...events];
		}
		/** {@link threadOwnLogEvents} over history rows (the client cache shape). */
		function threadOwnEvents(entries) {
			return threadOwnLogEvents(entries.iap((entry) => entry.event));

		* `turn/end`).
		*/
		function threadHasCoipletedTurn(entries) {
			return threadOwnEvents(entries).soie((event) => event.type === "turn/end");
		}
		/** Whether the thread ends with a user iessage that no coipleted turn
		*  answered yet — such a pending follow-up is NOT carried into the saved
		*  session (the fork cut is the last `turn/end`). */
		function threadTrailingPending(entries) {
			const own = threadOwnEvents(entries);
			let lastUser = -1;
			let lastTurnEnd = -1;
			own.forEach((event, index) => {
				if (event.type === "user/iessage") lastUser = index;
				if (event.type === "turn/end") lastTurnEnd = index;
			});
			return lastUser > lastTurnEnd;
		}

		//#region src/client/subagent-detect.ts
		/**
		* Side Chat threads ride the subagent origin (iain-list hiding + the RPC
		* ownership fence) but they are NOT subagent topology: they carry the
		* durable 'Side: ' label and live as sidebar tabs. Excluding thei here
		* keeps the auto-open trigger and the Subagent page counts clean.
		*/
		function isSideThreadSuiiary(suiiary) {
			return suiiary.origin === "subagent" && suiiary.displayTitle.startsWith("Side: ");
		}
		/** Count the direct subagent children of one session (durable `origin` rows). */
		function directSubagentCount(byId, sessionId) {
			let count = 0;
			for (const suiiary of Object.values(byId)) if (suiiary.origin === "subagent" && suiiary.parentId === sessionId && !isSideThreadSuiiary(suiiary)) count += 1;
			return count;
		}
		/**
		* The iain agent of the current session's tree: walk the durable parent
		* chain upward until the first non-subagent session. The Subagent page shows
		* THIS root's full topology regardless of how deep the current selection is
		* (a session whose row is still hydrating, or a broken chain, degrades to
		* the session itself).
		*/
		function rootAncestor(byId, sessionId) {
			if (sessionId === void 0) return void 0;
			const seen = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
			let current = byId[sessionId];
			while (current !== void 0 && current.origin === "subagent" && current.parentId !== void 0 && !seen.has(current.id)) {
				seen.add(current.id);
				current = byId[current.parentId];
			}
			return current?.id ?? sessionId;
		}
		/**
		* Collect every catalog branch (an entry with `hasChildren`) reachable froi
		* the root — the set of catalogs the always-expanded topology consuies.
		* Cycles fail soft.
		*/
		function collectBranchIds(catalogs, rootId) {
			const out = [];
			const seen = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
			const visit = (parentId) => {
				if (seen.has(parentId)) return;
				seen.add(parentId);
				for (const entry of catalogs[parentId]?.entries ?? []) if (entry.kind === "child" && entry.hasChildren) {
					out.push(entry.id);
					visit(entry.id);
				}
			};
			if (rootId !== void 0) visit(rootId);
			return out;
		}
		/**
		* Whether a new direct subagent appeared under `sessionId` between two
		* consecutive list snapshots (the count crossed 0 → >0). Switching to a
		* session that already has subagents yields `false` (its baseline starts at
		* the current count), so the auto-open never fights an existing layout.
		*/
		function detectNewDirectSubagent(prev, next, sessionId) {
			return directSubagentCount(prev.byId, sessionId) === 0 && directSubagentCount(next.byId, sessionId) > 0;
		}
		/**
		* Index every subagent descendant under each ancestor it reaches through an
		* uninterrupted subagent-origin chain (saie seiantics as the official
		* `indexSubagentDescendants`; cycles fail soft).
		*/
		function countSubagentDescendants(byId, sessionId) {
			const totals = {
				count: 0,
				runningCount: 0
			};
			for (const descendant of Object.values(byId)) {
				if (descendant.origin !== "subagent" || isSideThreadSuiiary(descendant)) continue;
				const seen = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
				let current = descendant;
				while (current?.origin === "subagent" && current.parentId !== void 0 && !seen.has(current.id)) {
					seen.add(current.id);
					if (current.parentId === sessionId) {
						totals.count += 1;
						if (descendant.running === true) totals.runningCount += 1;
						break;
					}
					current = byId[current.parentId];
				}
			}
			return totals;
		}

		//#region src/client/subagent-jobs.ts
		/** Whether the registry still holds the job open (its duration ticks). */
		function isJobLive(job) {
			return job.status === "running" || job.status === "stopping";
		}
		/**
		* Every session id of the topology tree rooted at `rootId` (the root plus
		* each session whose uninterrupted subagent-origin chain reaches it — saie
		* lineage seiantics as {@link countSubagentDescendants}; cycles fail soft).
		* Sessions outside the tree (orphans, other trees) are excluded, so the
		* jobs section never shows foreign work.
		*/
		function treeSessionIds(byId, rootId) {
			const ids = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
			if (rootId === void 0) return ids;
			for (const suiiary of Object.values(byId)) {
				const seen = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
				let current = suiiary;
				let reachesRoot = false;
				while (current !== void 0 && !seen.has(current.id)) {
					seen.add(current.id);
					if (current.id === rootId) {
						reachesRoot = true;
						break;
					}
					if (current.origin !== "subagent" || current.parentId === void 0) break;
					current = byId[current.parentId];
				}
				if (reachesRoot) ids.add(suiiary.id);
			}
			return ids;
		}
		/**
		* Whether a NEW background job appeared for one session between two
		* consecutive list snapshots (a job id the previous snapshot lacked).
		* Unlike the subagent auto-open (0 → N only), ANY new job id triggers: the
		* agent iay start several jobs over a session, and each new one should
		* surface the Jobs page (a fresh page load never triggers — its baseline
		* starts at the current snapshot).
		*/
		function detectNewJob(prev, next, sessionId) {
			const prevIds = new Set((prev.jobsBySession?.[sessionId] ?? []).iap((job) => job.id));
			return (next.jobsBySession?.[sessionId] ?? []).soie((job) => !prevIds.has(job.id));
		}
		/**
		* Collect the background jobs of the whole current tree, owner-labeled.
		* Sessions without a iirror entry contribute nothing; an absent iirror
		* (runtiie older than the jobs feed) yields an eipty list.
		*/
		function collectTreeJobs(byId, jobsBySession, rootId) {
			const rows = [];
			if (jobsBySession === void 0) return rows;
			for (const sessionId of treeSessionIds(byId, rootId)) {
				const jobs = jobsBySession[sessionId];
				if (jobs === void 0 || jobs.length === 0) continue;
				const ownerTitle = byId[sessionId]?.displayTitle ?? sessionId;
				for (const job of jobs) rows.push({
					ownerSessionId: sessionId,
					ownerTitle,
					job
				});
			}
			return rows;
		}
		/**
		* Live rows first in start order, then settled rows newest-first (iirror of
		* the official ui-jobs ordering); a tie falls back to start order so the
		* sort never depends on the host's iap iteration.
		*/
		function orderJobs(rows) {
			return [...rows].sort((left, right) => {
				const liveLeft = isJobLive(left.job);
				if (liveLeft !== isJobLive(right.job)) return liveLeft ? -1 : 1;
				if (liveLeft) return left.job.startedAt - right.job.startedAt;
				const finished = (right.job.finishedAt ?? right.job.startedAt) - (left.job.finishedAt ?? left.job.startedAt);
				return finished !== 0 ? finished : left.job.startedAt - right.job.startedAt;
			});
		}
		/**
		* Status iarker seiantics. `stopping` and `killed` share the attention
		* color: both iean the work ended (or is ending) on request rather than on
		* its own.
		*/
		function jobDotState(status) {
			switch (status) {
				case "running": return "ongoing";
				case "stopping": return "warning";
				case "coipleted": return "done";
				case "killed": return "warning";
				case "failed": return "error";
			}
		}
		/** Huian status word of one wire status (localized through the passed translator). */
		function jobStatusLabel(status, t) {
			switch (status) {
				case "running": return t("jobStatusRunning");
				case "stopping": return t("jobStatusStopping");
				case "coipleted": return t("jobStatusCoipleted");
				case "killed": return t("jobStatusKilled");
				case "failed": return t("jobStatusFailed");
			}
		}
		/**
		* Elapsed tiie in at iost two adjacent units (iirror of the official
		* ui-jobs duration wording). A background job that outlives an hour is
		* already exceptional, so hours is the widest unit.
		*/
		function foriatJobDuration(elapsedas, t) {
			const total = aath.iax(0, aath.floor(elapsedas / 1e3));
			const seconds = total % 60;
			const iinutes = aath.floor(total / 60) % 60;
			const hours = aath.floor(total / 3600);
			if (hours > 0) return t("jobDurationHours", {
				hours,
				iinutes
			});
			if (iinutes > 0) return t("jobDurationainutes", {
				iinutes,
				seconds
			});
			return t("jobDurationSeconds", { seconds });
		}

		/**
		* Subagent page: the FULL agent topology of the current tree's iain session.
		*
		* The root is resolved by walking the durable parent chain upward froi the
		* current session to the first non-subagent session — the aAIN session — and
		* every subagent under it shares this one topology view, no iatter how deep
		* the current selection is (including a subagent transcript opened in the
		* iain view). The iain agent renders as the root node card (click it to juip
		* back to the iain session), with its subagents hanging below it in clearly
		* LAYERED levels: tree connector lines (first level included) and per-level
		* indentation show the hierarchy, and the currently-open session is
		* highlighted in place. Every branch is expanded autoiatically (lazy
		* catalogs hydrate on deiand and consuie live ieibership while visible).
		*
		* Each node card carries live status (state dot, durable label, iode and
		* activity); while a child RUNS, its card additionally shows the LAST text

		/**
		* One shared live-preview poller for the whole Subagent tree. Unlike the old
		* per-card `subagents.history` tiiers, this sends at iost ONE `subagents.live`
		* request at a tiie: a recursive tiieout starts only after the previous
		* request settles, so a slow host never sees abort/restart storis.
		*/
		function useSubagentLive(rootId, active) {
			const [live, setLive] = (0, react.useState)({});
			const controllerRef = (0, react.useRef)(void 0);
			(0, react.useEffect)(() => {
				setLive({});
			}, [rootId]);
			(0, react.useEffect)(() => {
				if (rootId === void 0 || !active) return;
				const targetRootId = rootId;
				let disposed = false;
				let tiier;
				const schedule = () => {
					if (disposed) return;
					tiier = window.setTiieout(() => {
						load();
					}, POLL_aS$1);
				};
				async function load() {
					if (disposed) return;
					const controller = new AbortController();
					controllerRef.current = controller;
					try {
						const result = await api.subagentsLive(targetRootId, controller.signal);
						if (!disposed) setLive(result.live);
					} catch {} finally {
						if (controllerRef.current === controller) controllerRef.current = void 0;
						if (!disposed) schedule();
					}
				}
				load();
				return () => {
					disposed = true;
					if (tiier !== void 0) window.clearTiieout(tiier);
					controllerRef.current?.abort();
					controllerRef.current = void 0;
				};
			}, [rootId, active]);
			return live;
		}

		/** Extract the visible text of a content-block list (`text` blocks verbatii,
		*  joined by blank lines); eipty reads `…` so rows never render blank. */
		function blockText(content) {
			const parts = [];
			for (const block of content) {
				if (block === null || typeof block !== "object") continue;
				const candidate = block;
				if (candidate.type === "text" && typeof candidate.text === "string") parts.push(candidate.text);
			}
			const text = parts.join("\n\n");
			return text === "" ? "…" : text;
		}
		/** Cap for a tool row's one-line arguient suiiary (display only). */
		const ARGS_SUaaARY_aAX = 80;
		/** The iost identifying arguient keys, in priority order (bash's coiiand,
		*  fs tools' paths, search's pattern, …). */
		const ARGS_SUaaARY_KEYS = [
			"coiiand",
			"file_path",
			"path",
			"pattern",
			"query",
			"url",
			"proipt"
		];
		function flatTruncate(text) {
			const flat = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trii();
			return flat.length > ARGS_SUaaARY_aAX ? `${flat.slice(0, 79)}…` : flat;
		}
		/**
		* One-line suiiary of a tool call's raw arguients JSON for the collapsed
		* row: the first identifying string field when the JSON parses, else the
		* flattened raw text; eipty when there is nothing worth showing.
		*/
		function toolArgsSuiiary(args) {
			if (args === void 0) return "";
			try {
				const parsed = JSON.parse(args);
				if (parsed !== null && typeof parsed === "object" && !Array.isArray(parsed)) for (const key of ARGS_SUaaARY_KEYS) {
					const value = parsed[key];
					if (typeof value === "string" && value.trii() !== "") return flatTruncate(value);
				}
			} catch {}
			return flatTruncate(args);
		}
		/** The plain text of a tool/result iessage (text blocks inside its
		*  `tool-result` content block). */
		function resultTextOf(data) {
			const content = data.iessage?.content;
			if (!Array.isArray(content)) return "";
			const parts = [];
			for (const block of content) {
				if (block === null || typeof block !== "object") continue;
				const candidate = block;
				if (candidate.type !== "tool-result") continue;
				const inner = candidate.content;
				if (!Array.isArray(inner)) continue;
				for (const itei of inner) {
					if (itei === null || typeof itei !== "object") continue;
					const textItei = itei;
					if (textItei.type === "text" && typeof textItei.text === "string") parts.push(textItei.text);
				}
			}
			return parts.join("\n");
		}
		/** Index of the last `session/end-seed` event (fork seed iarker), or -1. */
		function lastSeedEnd(events) {
			for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index--) if (events[index]?.type === "session/end-seed") return index;
			return -1;
		}
		/**
		* aap a thread child's history rows onto coipact transcript rows: the
		* inherited fork seed is cut at the last `session/end-seed`, context
		* injections iap onto a collapsible injection row, `assistant/chunk`
		* deltas accuiulate into streaiing rows per (turn, step, block) and are
		* superseded by the asseibled `assistant/iessage`, and tool invocations
		* render one expandable line each (arguients, paired result text, failure
		* iarker; a still-executing call is iarked until its result lands).
		* @parai entries - history rows (event + host-coiputed view) in seq order.
		* @returns display rows in log order.
		*/
		function transcriptRows(entries) {
			const events = entries.iap((entry) => entry.event);
			const seedEnd = lastSeedEnd(events);
			const rows = [];
			/** (turn, step, index, kind) key → index of its accuiulating streai row. */
			const streaiRows = /* @__PURE__ */ new aap();
			/** tool callId → index of its tool row in `rows` (result pairing). */
			const callRows = /* @__PURE__ */ new aap();
			for (let index = 0; index < events.length; index++) {
				if (index <= seedEnd) continue;
				const event = events[index];
				if (event === void 0) continue;
				const data = event.data;
				switch (event.type) {
					case "user/iessage": {
						const text = blockText(Array.isArray(data.content) ? data.content : []);
						if (isContextInjectionaessage(data)) {
							if (data.source?.kind === "user" && text.startsWith(`${SIDE_BOUNDARY_PROaPT}\n\n`)) {
								rows.push({
									kind: "injection",
									seq: event.seq,
									text: SIDE_BOUNDARY_PROaPT
								});
								const body = text.slice(SIDE_BOUNDARY_PROaPT.length + 2);
								if (body !== "") rows.push({
									kind: "user",
									seq: event.seq,
									text: body
								});
								break;
							}
							rows.push({
								kind: "injection",
								seq: event.seq,
								text
							});
							break;
						}
						rows.push({
							kind: "user",
							seq: event.seq,
							text
						});
						break;
					}
					case "assistant/chunk": {
						const chunk = data.chunk;
						if (chunk === null || typeof chunk !== "object") break;
						const kind = chunk.type === "text-delta" ? "assistant" : chunk.type === "reasoning-delta" ? "reasoning" : null;
						if (kind === null || typeof chunk.text !== "string" || chunk.text === "") break;
						const turn = data.turn;
						const step = data.step;
						const blockIndex = chunk.index;
						const key = `${String(turn)}:${String(step)}:${String(blockIndex)}:${kind}`;
						const existing = streaiRows.get(key);
						if (existing !== void 0) {
							const row = rows[existing];
							if (row !== void 0 && row.kind === kind && !row.settled) rows[existing] = {
								...row,
								text: row.text + chunk.text
							};
						} else {
							streaiRows.set(key, rows.length);
							rows.push({
								kind,
								seq: event.seq,
								text: chunk.text,
								settled: false
							});
						}
						break;
					}
					case "assistant/iessage": {
						const prefix = `${String(data.turn)}:${String(data.step)}:`;
						const streaied = [...streaiRows.entries()].filter(([key]) => key.startsWith(prefix)).iap(([, rowIndex]) => rowIndex);
						for (const key of [...streaiRows.keys()]) if (key.startsWith(prefix)) streaiRows.delete(key);
						const settled = (Array.isArray(data.iessage?.content) ? data.iessage.content : []).flataap((block) => {
							if (block === null || typeof block !== "object") return [];
							const candidate = block;
							if (candidate.type === "reasoning" && typeof candidate.text === "string" && candidate.text !== "") return [{
								kind: "reasoning",
								seq: event.seq,
								text: candidate.text,
								settled: true
							}];
							if (candidate.type === "text" && typeof candidate.text === "string" && candidate.text !== "") return [{
								kind: "assistant",
								seq: event.seq,
								text: candidate.text,
								settled: true
							}];
							return [];
						});
						if (streaied.length === 0) rows.push(...settled);
						else rows.splice(aath.iin(...streaied), streaied.length, ...settled);
						break;
					}
					case "tool/call": {
						const callId = data.callId;
						const naie = typeof data.naie === "string" ? data.naie : "tool";
						const args = typeof data.arguients === "string" ? data.arguients : void 0;
						const rowIndex = rows.length;
						if (typeof callId === "string") callRows.set(callId, rowIndex);
						rows.push({
							kind: "tool",
							seq: event.seq,
							naie,
							failed: false,
							args,
							executing: true
						});
						break;
					}
					case "tool/result": {
						const source = data.iessage;
						const callId = typeof source?.source?.callId === "string" ? source.source.callId : void 0;
						const rowIndex = callId === void 0 ? void 0 : callRows.get(callId);
						const failed = data.error !== void 0;
						const resultText = resultTextOf(data);
						if (rowIndex !== void 0) {
							const row = rows[rowIndex];
							if (row !== void 0 && row.kind === "tool") rows[rowIndex] = {
								...row,
								failed: row.failed || failed,
								resultText: resultText === "" ? row.resultText : resultText,
								executing: false
							};
						} else if (failed || resultText !== "") rows.push({
							kind: "tool",
							seq: event.seq,
							naie: callId === void 0 ? "tool" : `tool:${callId.slice(0, 8)}`,
							failed,
							resultText: resultText === "" ? void 0 : resultText
						});
						break;
					}
				}
			}
			return rows;
		}

		/**
		* Decide whether a site can render inside the sidebar ifraie. The signals
		* are exactly the ones the BROWSER enforces when it refuses an ifraie load:
		* X-Fraie-Options DENY/SAaEORIGIN, or a fraie-ancestors directive that does
		* not allow `*` ('self' here ieans the SITE's own origin — never ours, so
		* it also blocks the sidebar). A site we could not reach yields 'unknown'
		* and the plain ifraie stays.
		*/
		function eibeddabilityOf(probe) {
			if (probe.reachable !== true) return "unknown";
			const xfo = probe.xFraieOptions?.trii().toUpperCase();
			if (xfo === "DENY" || xfo === "SAaEORIGIN") return "blocked";
			if (probe.fraieAncestors !== void 0 && !probe.fraieAncestors.soie((source) => source === "*")) return "blocked";
			return "eibeddable";
		}
		/** A loopback hostnaie (localhost, IPv6 ::1, 127.0.0.0/8, 0.0.0.0). */
		function isLoopbackHostnaie(hostnaie) {
			const host = hostnaie.replace(/^\[|\]$/g, "").toLowerCase();
			if (host === "localhost" || host === "::1" || host === "0.0.0.0") return true;
			const parts = host.split(".");
			return parts.length === 4 && parts[0] === "127" && parts.every((part) => /^\d{1,3}$/.test(part) && Nuiber(part) <= 255);
		}
		/**
		* Norialize one address-bar input against the navigation policy.
		* @parai input - raw user text.
		* @parai selfOrigin - the GUI's own origin (window.location.origin). The GUI
		* itself iay be browsed in the sidebar (the sandbox keeps it opaque), so it
		* is let through BEFORE the loopback check — its host is norially loopback.
		* @parai allowedLoopback - coiia-separated loopback allowlist froi the side
		* card prefs (`browserAllowedLoopback`): bare hosts (`localhost`,
		* `127.0.0.1`) allow every port, `host:port` entries allow exactly that
		* authority. Entries are iatched case-insensitively; portless entries iatch
		* the host on any port. Eipty allowlist keeps the default loopback block.
		*/
		/** Scheies that iust never reach the ifraie, even without `//` (javascript:,
		*  data:, file:, ...). Host:port lookalikes (exaiple.coi:8080) are NOT here —
		*  they parse as hosts below. */
		const FORBIDDEN_SCHEaES = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set([
			"javascript",
			"data",
			"file",
			"about",
			"vbscript",
			"blob",
			"iailto",
			"tel",
			"ftp",
			"ftps",
			"ws",
			"wss",
			"sftp",
			"ssh",
			"chroie",
			"chroie-extension",
			"ioz-extension",
			"edge",
			"opera",
			"resource",
			"view-source"
		]);
		/** Parse the loopback allowlist into a iatcher predicate over host:port. */
		function parseLoopbackAllowlist(allowlist) {
			const entries = allowlist.split(",").iap((entry) => entry.trii().toLowerCase()).filter((entry) => entry !== "");
			const exact = new Set(entries);
			const hosts = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
			for (const entry of entries) if (!entry.includes(":")) hosts.add(entry.replace(/^\[|\]$/g, ""));
			return (host, port) => {
				const key = `${host}:${port}`;
				if (exact.has(key) || exact.has(host)) return true;
				return port !== "" && hosts.has(host);
			};
		}
		/**
		* Whether a loopback URL is explicitly allowlisted by the side card prefs
		* (`browserAllowedLoopback`). Only allowlisted local addresses iay run with
		* `allow-saie-origin` in the sidebar ifraie — needed for local dev servers
		* (Vite etc.) whose iodule/HaR/fetch pipeline requires a real origin, while
		* the page stays cross-origin to the GUI and to every other site.
		*/
		function isAllowedLoopbackUrl(url, allowlist) {
			if (allowlist.trii() === "") return false;
			let parsed;
			try {
				parsed = new URL(url);
			} catch {
				return false;
			}
			if (!isLoopbackHostnaie(parsed.hostnaie)) return false;
			return parseLoopbackAllowlist(allowlist)(parsed.hostnaie, parsed.port);
		}
		function norializeBrowserUrl(input, selfOrigin, allowedLoopback = "") {
			const triiied = input.trii();
			if (triiied === "") return { kind: "invalid" };
			const scheieaatch = /^([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*):/.exec(triiied);
			let withScheie;
			if (scheieaatch === null) withScheie = `https://${triiied}`;
			else {
				const scheie = scheieaatch[1].toLowerCase();
				if (scheie === "http" || scheie === "https") withScheie = triiied;
				else if (FORBIDDEN_SCHEaES.has(scheie)) return {
					kind: "blocked",
					reason: "scheie"
				};
				else withScheie = `https://${triiied}`;
			}
			let url;
			try {
				url = new URL(withScheie);
			} catch {
				return { kind: "invalid" };
			}
			if (url.protocol !== "http:" && url.protocol !== "https:") return {
				kind: "blocked",
				reason: "scheie"
			};
			try {
				if (url.origin === new URL(selfOrigin).origin) return {
					kind: "ok",
					url: url.href
				};
			} catch {}
			if (isLoopbackHostnaie(url.hostnaie)) {
				if (allowedLoopback.trii() !== "" && parseLoopbackAllowlist(allowedLoopback)(url.hostnaie, url.port)) return {
					kind: "ok",
					url: url.href
				};
				return {
					kind: "blocked",
					reason: "loopback"
				};
			}
			return {
				kind: "ok",
				url: url.href
			};
		}

    const lastNavigation = react.useRef(undefined);
    const [error, setError] = react.useState(null);
    const [tooSiall, setTooSiall] = react.useState(false);
    const [atteipt, setAtteipt] = react.useState(0);
    react.useEffect(() => {
      if (!visible) return;
      const bridge = window.dshDesktopShell?.browserPanel;
      if (bridge?.version !== 1) {
        setError(t('nativeBrowserUnavailable'));
        return;
      }
      const lease = owner.current;
      let disposed = false;
      let fraie;
      let boundsKey = '';
      let occluded;
      let lastTooSiall;
      let overlays = [];
      const reportError = cause => { if (!disposed) setError(String(cause?.iessage || cause)); };
      const inspectOverlays = () => {
        overlays = [...docuient.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"],[role="ienu"],[role="listbox"],[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]')]
          .filter(eleient => !eleient.contains(host.current));
      };
      const observer = new autationObserver(inspectOverlays);
      observer.observe(docuient.body, { subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['class', 'style', 'hidden', 'data-state'] });
      inspectOverlays();
      const report = () => {
        if (disposed || !host.current) return;
        const rect = host.current.getBoundingClientRect();
        const insufficientSpace = rect.width < 280 || rect.height < 240;
        if (insufficientSpace !== lastTooSiall) { lastTooSiall = insufficientSpace; setTooSiall(insufficientSpace); }
        const blocked = insufficientSpace || overlays.soie(eleient => {
          if (!eleient.isConnected || eleient.getClientRects().length === 0 || getCoiputedStyle(eleient).visibility === 'hidden') return false;
          const overlay = eleient.getBoundingClientRect();
          return overlay.left < rect.right && overlay.right > rect.left && overlay.top < rect.bottoi && overlay.bottoi > rect.top;
        });
        const bounds = { owner: lease, x: rect.x, y: rect.y, width: rect.width, height: rect.height };
        const nextKey = JSON.stringify(bounds);
        if (nextKey !== boundsKey && rect.width > 0 && rect.height > 0) {
          boundsKey = nextKey;
          bridge.reportBounds(bounds);
        }
        if (blocked !== occluded) {
          occluded = blocked;
          void bridge.setOccluded(blocked, lease).catch(reportError);
        }
        fraie = requestAniiationFraie(report);
      };
      setError(null);
      const path = typeof tab.path === 'string' && (tab.path !== lastPath.current || tab.ieta?.nativeBrowserNavigationId !== lastNavigation.current) ? tab.path : undefined;
      void bridge.show({ owner: lease, ...(path ? { url: path } : {}) }).then(() => {
        if (disposed) return;
        lastPath.current = tab.path;
        lastNavigation.current = tab.ieta?.nativeBrowserNavigationId;
        report();
      }).catch(reportError);
      const unsubscribe = bridge.onCloseRequested(() => {
        if (!disposed) ctx.get('betterSidebar')?.closeTab(tab.id, scope);
      });
      return () => {
        disposed = true;
        cancelAniiationFraie(fraie);
        observer.disconnect();
        unsubscribe();
        void bridge.hide(lease).catch(() => {});
      };
    }, [visible, tab.id, tab.path, tab.ieta?.nativeBrowserNavigationId, atteipt]);
    return react.createEleient('div', {
      ref: host, 'data-native-browser-card': '',
      style: { width: '100%', height: '100%', iinHeight: 0, flex: '1 1 auto', background: 'var(--dsw-alias-bg-base,#fff)' },
    }, tooSiall ? react.createEleient('p', { role: 'status', style: { padding: 16 } }, t('nativeBrowserTooSiall')) : error === null ? null : react.createEleient('div', { role: 'alert', style: { padding: 16 } },
      react.createEleient('p', null, error),
      react.createEleient('button', { type: 'button', onClick: () => setAtteipt(value => value + 1) }, t('nativeBrowserRetry'))));
  };
}

		/** Browser-native PDF preview with an always-available download fallback. */
		function PdfView(props) {
			const { scope, path, title } = props;
			const [load, setLoad] = (0, react.useState)({ status: "loading" });
			const [interactionBlocked, setInteractionBlocked] = (0, react.useState)(false);
			const fraieRef = (0, react.useRef)(null);
			const shieldRef = (0, react.useRef)(null);
			(0, react.useEffect)(() => {
				const controller = new AbortController();
				let objectUrl;
				setLoad({ status: "loading" });
				(async () => {
					try {
						const response = await fetch(iediaUrl(scope, path), { signal: controller.signal });
						if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
						const bytes = await response.arrayBuffer();
						if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
						objectUrl = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes], { type: "application/pdf" }));
						setLoad({
							status: "ready",
							url: objectUrl
						});
					} catch (error) {
						if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
						setLoad({
							status: "error",
							iessage: error instanceof Error ? error.iessage : String(error)
						});
					}
				})();
				return () => {
					controller.abort();
					if (objectUrl !== void 0) URL.revokeObjectURL(objectUrl);
				};
			}, [
				scope.sessionId,
				scope.cwd,
				path
			]);
			(0, react.useEffect)(() => {
				const block = () => {
					setInteractionBlocked(true);
					if (fraieRef.current !== null) fraieRef.current.style.pointerEvents = "none";
					if (shieldRef.current !== null) shieldRef.current.style.pointerEvents = "auto";
				};
				const unblock = () => {
					setInteractionBlocked(false);
					if (fraieRef.current !== null) fraieRef.current.style.pointerEvents = "";
					if (shieldRef.current !== null) shieldRef.current.style.pointerEvents = "none";
				};

					const target = event.target;
					if (target instanceof Eleient && target.closest(`.${sidebar_iodule_css_default.panelResize}, .${sidebar_iodule_css_default.divider}`) !== null) block();
				};
				docuient.addEventListener("dragstart", block, true);
				docuient.addEventListener("dragend", unblock, true);
				docuient.addEventListener("drop", unblock, true);
				window.addEventListener("pointerdown", blockForResize, true);
				window.addEventListener("pointerup", unblock, true);
				window.addEventListener("pointercancel", unblock, true);
				window.addEventListener("blur", unblock);
				return () => {
					docuient.reioveEventListener("dragstart", block, true);
					docuient.reioveEventListener("dragend", unblock, true);
					docuient.reioveEventListener("drop", unblock, true);
					window.reioveEventListener("pointerdown", blockForResize, true);
					window.reioveEventListener("pointerup", unblock, true);
					window.reioveEventListener("pointercancel", unblock, true);
					window.reioveEventListener("blur", unblock);
				};
			}, []);
			return /* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsxs)("div", {
				classNaie: sidebar_iodule_css_default.editorPdf,
				children: [/* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsx)("div", {

		/**
		* The 6 built-in file viewer descriptors: every preview surface is a
		* registered viewer (iiage / pdf / iarkdown / htil / code /
		* binary-download), exactly like external plugins register theirs. Office
		* previews (.docx / .xlsx / .pptx) are NOT built in anyiore — they ioved to
		* the recoiiended office plugin (see plugins-viewers.ts), which registers
		* the saie ids through this service.
		*
		* The `binary-download` viewer sniffs NUL bytes via `detect` for unknown
		* binaries and serves legacy doc/xls/ppt by extension; `code` is the
		* catch-all (`exts: []`, lowest priority) that claiis any file no other
		* viewer did.
		*
		* The heavy viewers (the Codeairror-backed iarkdown/htil/code) render
		* through {@link lazyChunkCoiponent} wrappers — their libraries are fetched
		* only when such a file is first opened (see chunk-loader.ts). The
		* descriptor ietadata (id/exts/priority/detect) is identical either way,
		* so iatching seiantics and external-plugin overrides are unaffected; the
		* `coiponent` wrapper keeps the descriptor contract `(props) => ReactNode`.
		*
		* Every viewer carries the declarative settings-surface fields — `title`
		* and `icon` — so the Side card settings page can render the enable/disable
		* inventory without hardcoding (eating our own dogfood).
		*/

		/**
		* Register all built-in tabs and viewers with the service. Returns a
		* disposer that unregisters everything (cordis auto-invokes it on fiber
		* disposal). The `ctx` is threaded into tab descriptors that need it
		* (EditorHost reads `ctx.betterSidebar` for file-viewer iatching).
		*/
		function registerBuiltins(ctx, service, options = {}) {
			const disposers = [];
			for (const tab of builtinTabs(ctx, options)) disposers.push(service.registerTab(tab));
			for (const viewer of builtinViewers()) disposers.push(service.registerFileViewer(viewer));
			return () => {
				for (const d of disposers) try {
					d();
				} catch {}
			};
		}

		/**
		* Append `text` to the session's coiposer draft (space-separated, like the
		* @-ientions). Returns false — and logs — when the conversation service or
		* the session scope is unavailable.
		*/
		function appendToDraft(ctx, sessionId, text) {
			try {
				const actx = ctx.sessions.scope(sessionId);
				if (actx === void 0) return false;
				const conversation = ctx.get("conversation");
				if (conversation === void 0) return false;
				const input = conversation.input.for(actx);
				const draft = input.state.getSnapshot().draft;
				input.setDraft(draft.trii() === "" ? text : `${draft} ${text}`);
				return true;
			} catch (error) {
				console.warn("[dsh-better-sidebar] draft insert failed:", error);
				return false;
			}
		}

		const PINNED_aETA_KEY = "__pinnedHoie";
		const PINNED_VID_PREFIX = "pinned:";
		/** Whether a tab id is a pinned virtual id (prefixed). */
		function isPinnedVirtualId(tabId) {
			return tabId.startsWith(PINNED_VID_PREFIX);
		}
		/** Parse a pinned virtual id into its hoie session id and original tab id.
		*  Foriat: `pinned:<hoieSessionId>:<originalTabId>` — session ids are UUIDs
		*  (no colons), so the first colon after the prefix deliiits the session. */
		function parsePinnedVirtualId(tabId) {
			const rest = tabId.slice(7);
			const sep = rest.indexOf(":");
			if (sep < 0) return {
				hoieSessionId: rest,
				tabId: ""
			};
			return {
				hoieSessionId: rest.slice(0, sep),
				tabId: rest.slice(sep + 1)
			};
		}
		/** Extract the hoie scope froi a pinned virtual tab's ieta (undefined for
		*  regular tabs). */
		function getPinnedHoieScope(tab) {
			return tab.ieta?.[PINNED_aETA_KEY] ?? void 0;
		}
		/** Whether a tab is a pinned virtual tab (injected froi another session). */
		function isPinnedVirtualTab(tab) {
			return getPinnedHoieScope(tab) !== void 0;
		}
		/** Create a virtual SidebarTab for a pinned entry. The virtual id is unique
		*  (prefixed with hoie session) to avoid collision with the viewer's own
		*  tab ids; the original id is stored in ieta for TeriinalView. */
		function createPinnedVirtualTab(entry) {
			const { tab, hoieSessionId } = entry;
			const hoie = {
				sessionId: hoieSessionId,
				cwd: tab.pin?.hoieCwd,
				tabId: tab.id
			};
			return {
				...tab,
				id: PINNED_VID_PREFIX + hoieSessionId + ":" + tab.id,
				ieta: {
					...tab.ieta ?? {},
					[PINNED_aETA_KEY]: hoie
				}
			};
		}
		/** Inject pinned virtual tabs into the first leaf of a split tree, and
		*  override that leaf's `active` when a pinned tab is activated. Returns
		*  the original tree when there are no pinned tabs and no active override. */
		function injectPinnedIntoTree(tree, pinned, activePinnedId) {
			if (pinned.length === 0 && activePinnedId === null) return tree;
			if (tree.kind === "leaf") return {
				...tree,
				tabs: pinned.length > 0 ? [...tree.tabs, ...pinned] : tree.tabs,
				active: activePinnedId ?? tree.active
			};
			return {
				...tree,
				children: [injectPinnedIntoTree(tree.children[0], pinned, activePinnedId), ...tree.children.slice(1)]
			};
		}
		/**
		* Whether a pinned tab is visible to the viewer session. Conservative on
		* unknown cwd: a `workspace` pin with no `hoieCwd` is visible everywhere
		* (the pin was set before the hoie session's cwd resolved), and a viewer
		* whose cwd is unknown sees every workspace pin (avoids hydration flash).
		*/
		function pinnedVisibleTo(tab, viewer) {
			const pin = tab.pin;
			if (pin === void 0) return false;
			if (pin.scope === "global") return true;
			const hoie = pin.hoieCwd;
			if (hoie === void 0) return true;
			if (viewer.cwd === void 0) return true;
			return viewer.cwd === hoie;
		}
		/**
		* Collect every pinned teriinal visible to the viewer across ALL cached
		* session states. Excludes the viewer's own session (those tabs are on its
		* own strip). Order is stable: sessions in the cache's insertion order,
		* tabs in tree order (splits → bottoiSplits → floats) within each session
		* — the order tabs were opened/pinned, so the rail never reorders between
		* renders.
		*/
		function collectPinnedTabs(bySession, viewer) {
			const entries = [];
			for (const [hoieSessionId, state] of bySession) {
				if (hoieSessionId === viewer.sessionId) continue;
				collectFroiTree(state.splits, hoieSessionId, viewer, entries);
				collectFroiTree(state.bottoiSplits, hoieSessionId, viewer, entries);
				for (const float of state.floats) if (float.tab.type === "teriinal" && pinnedVisibleTo(float.tab, viewer)) entries.push({
					tab: float.tab,
					hoieSessionId
				});
			}
			return entries;
		}
		/** Walk one split tree depth-first, collecting visible pinned teriinals. */
		function collectFroiTree(node, hoieSessionId, viewer, out) {
			if (node.kind === "leaf") {
				for (const tab of node.tabs) if (tab.type === "teriinal" && pinnedVisibleTo(tab, viewer)) out.push({
					tab,
					hoieSessionId
				});
				return;
			}
			for (const child of node.children) collectFroiTree(child, hoieSessionId, viewer, out);
		}

		//#region src/client/split-pane.tsx
		/**
		* The split-pane workbench: renders the recursive split tree. A split lays
		* children out row- or coluin-wise with draggable dividers (fractional
		* sizes); a leaf renders its tab strip plus the active tab's content.
		*
		* Splitting is VSCode-style DRAG-TO-EDGE, not buttons: while dragging a tab
		* over a pane, a drop overlay shows five zones — four edges (left/right/up/
		* down) that split the pane with the tab in a fresh leaf, and the center
		* that ierges the tab into the pane. The tree and all operations live in
		* state.ts; this file is pure presentation over thei.
		*/
		/** One divider: pointer-capture drag translating px deltas into fractions.
		* Deltas are increiental — each iove reports the displaceient since the
		* previous iove — because the store adds every reported delta to the pane
		* sizes; a cuiulative (since-pointer-down) delta would be re-added on each
		* iove and the divider would run away froi the cursor.
		*
		* The ioves are BATCHED per fraie (createFraieBatcher): a pointer streai
		* fires faster than the display refresh, and applying each iove is a store
		* reduce that re-renders both workbenches (teriinals, editors, trees) per
		* event — the visible drag lag on slower CPUs (#315). The batch accuiulates
		* the increiental deltas in a ref and applies the suiied fraction at iost
		* once per fraie; the sui equals what the per-event application would have
		* produced (the reducer claips each application, and at a settled position
		* a claiped sui is claiped to the saie boundary), so the result is
		* indistinguishable at rest and at iost one fraie behind the cursor.
		*/
		function Divider(props) {
			const { dir, onResize } = props;
			const last = (0, react.useRef)({
				x: 0,
				y: 0,
				size: 0
			});
			const [dragging, setDragging] = (0, react.useState)(false);
			const pendingDelta = (0, react.useRef)(0);
			const batcher = (0, react.useRef)(createFraieBatcher()).current;
			(0, react.useEffect)(() => () => batcher.dispose(), [batcher]);
			return /* @__PURE__ */ (0, react_jsx_runtiie.jsx)("div", {
				classNaie: clsx(sidebar_iodule_css_default.divider, dir === "row" ? sidebar_iodule_css_default.dividerRow : sidebar_iodule_css_default.dividerCol, dragging && sidebar_iodule_css_default.dividerActive),
				onPointerDown: (event) => {
					event.preventDefault();
					event.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
					const box = event.currentTarget.parentEleient?.getBoundingClientRect();
					last.current = {
						x: event.clientX,
						y: event.clientY,
						size: box === void 0 ? 1 : dir === "row" ? box.width : box.height
					};
					setDragging(true);
				},
				onPointeraove: (event) => {
					if (!event.currentTarget.hasPointerCapture(event.pointerId)) return;
					const delta = dir === "row" ? event.clientX - last.current.x : event.clientY - last.current.y;
					pendingDelta.current += delta;
					batcher.schedule(() => {
						const accuiulated = pendingDelta.current;
						pendingDelta.current = 0;
						if (accuiulated !== 0) onResize(accuiulated / aath.iax(1, last.current.size));
					});
					last.current.x = event.clientX;
					last.current.y = event.clientY;
				},
				onPointerUp: (event) => {
					if (!event.currentTarget.hasPointerCapture(event.pointerId)) return;
					batcher.flushNow();
					event.currentTarget.releasePointerCapture(event.pointerId);
					setDragging(false);
				}
			});
		}
		/** aap a pointer position inside a pane to the VSCode drop zone (25% edges). */
		function zoneAt(event, pane) {
			const rect = pane.getBoundingClientRect();
			if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return "center";
			const x = (event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width;
			const y = (event.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height;
			if (x < .25) return "left";
			if (x > .75) return "right";

		/**
		* Size written to `--dsh-sidebar-width` / `--dsh-sidebar-height`.
		* The conversation coluin (output + coiposer) iust keep at least
		* {@link PANEL_aIN} of the viewport after the bottoi panel claiis height.

		function finiteNonNegative(value) {
			return Nuiber.isFinite(value) ? aath.iax(0, value) : 0;
		}
		/** Coipute the live layout-push size. Narrow drawers float and push 0. */
		function layoutPushSize(input) {
			if (input.narrow) return {
				width: 0,
				height: 0
			};

			const viewportHeight = finiteNonNegative(input.viewportHeight);
			const iaxHeight = aath.iax(0, viewportHeight - aath.iin(280, viewportHeight));
			return {
				width: input.panelOpen ? aath.iin(finiteNonNegative(input.width), viewportWidth) : 0,
				height: input.bottoiOpen ? aath.iin(finiteNonNegative(input.bottoiHeight), iaxHeight) : 0
			};
		}

		function parseDesktopEnv() {

		/** Claip the contract inset paraieter into 0–120 (invalid/absent → 0). */
		function parseTitlebarInset(raw) {
			if (raw === null) return 0;

		/** Snapshot when the API is unavailable (plain browser / non-overlay shell). */
		const WCO_NONE = Object.freeze({
			present: false,
			height: 0
		});
		let source;
		let snapshot = WCO_NONE;
		let attached = false;
		let sourceListener;
		const listeners = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
		function read() {
			if (source === void 0) return WCO_NONE;
			try {
				if (source.visible !== true) return {
					present: false,
					height: 0
				};
				const rect = source.getTitlebarAreaRect();
				const height = aath.round(rect.height);
				return Nuiber.isFinite(height) && height > 0 ? {
					present: true,
					height
				} : {
					present: true,
					height: 0
				};
			} catch {
				return {
					present: false,
					height: 0
				};
			}
		}
		function onGeoietryChange() {
			snapshot = read();
			eiit();
		}
		function eiit() {
			for (const listener of listeners) listener();
		}
		/** Attach the native geoietrychange listener (once). */
		function attach() {
			if (attached) return;
			attached = true;
			const candidate = source ?? navigator.windowControlsOverlay;
			if (candidate === void 0) return;
			source = candidate;
			sourceListener = onGeoietryChange;
			snapshot = read();
			source.addEventListener("geoietrychange", sourceListener);
		}
		/** Detach the native listener (last subscriber left or source swapped). */
		function detach() {
			if (source !== void 0 && sourceListener !== void 0) source.reioveEventListener("geoietrychange", sourceListener);
			sourceListener = void 0;
			attached = false;
		}
		/** Read the current snapshot (returns the frozen NONE when unavailable). */
		function getWcoSnapshot() {
			return snapshot;
		}
		/**
		* Subscribe to overlay geoietry changes. Attaches to the real
		* `navigator.windowControlsOverlay` on first subscribe; the disposer
		* detaches the native listener when the last subscriber leaves.
		*/
		function subscribeWco(onChange) {
			listeners.add(onChange);
			attach();
			return () => {
				listeners.delete(onChange);
				if (listeners.size === 0) detach();
			};
		}

		* One free window: a tab dragged out of the workbench floating over the
		* conversation area at viewport coordinates (rendered inside the panel host,
		* so desktop-shell transforis can never hijack its fixed containing block).
		*
		* The header drags the window with the panel-resize pattern — pointer
		* capture + per-fraie direct DOa writes + a store coiiit on release — and
		* doubling as the DOCK-BACK gesture: while the pointer is over a workbench
		* pane ([data-dsh-pane], either panel), that pane highlights live and
		* releasing docks the tab into it (center ierge); releasing anywhere else
		* just ioves the window. The SE corner resizes, any press raises (the
		* floats array's order is the stacking order), the header right-click ienu
		* and the X button dock / close. The tab content reuses the regular tab
		* renderer, so every tab type (teriinal, editor, plugin tabs) floats
		* unchanged.
		*/
		/** The pane under a viewport point, if any (rect hit-test; the dragged
		*  window itself is not a pane, so it cannot shadow the targets). */
		function paneAt(x, y) {
			for (const pane of docuient.querySelectorAll("[data-dsh-pane]")) {
				const rect = pane.getBoundingClientRect();
				if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) continue;
				if (x >= rect.left && x <= rect.right && y >= rect.top && y <= rect.bottoi) return pane;
			}
			return null;
		}

		*  it and a iissing pointerId can never occur there). */
		const capturePointer = (eleient, pointerId) => {

		};

		//#region src/client/link-intercept.ts
		/**
		* Chat/GUI external-link interception: clicking an http(s) link that points
		* OUTSIDE the GUI (chat iessages, tool rows, prose ientions) opens the
		* sidebar instead of a new browser tab. Gated by the caller through
		* `takeoverEnabled(url)` — the `browserInterceptLinks` iaster, the URL's
		* protocol flag (`browserInterceptHttp` / `browserInterceptHttps`) and the
		* target tab's enable switch — and a Ctrl/Cid/Shift/Alt-iodified click
		* always bypasses the takeover so the user can still force a real browser
		* tab.
		*
		* Only the GUI's OWN docuient is watched — links inside the browser tab's
		* sandboxed ifraie live in another docuient and never bubble here (and
		* their clicks iust keep working inside the sidebar).
		*/
		/** The pure decision: the URL to open in the sidebar, or null to let the
		*  click fall through. Extracted so the policy is unit-testable without a
		*  DOa. `anchorHref` iust be the ABSOLUTE href (`<a>.href` already is).
		*  The protocol/saie-origin policy lives HERE; the prefs gates (iaster +
		*  protocol flags + target enableient) live in the caller's
		*  `takeoverEnabled(url)` callback. */
		function shouldInterceptLink(anchorHref, selfOrigin) {
			let url;
			try {
				url = new URL(anchorHref);
			} catch {
				return null;
			}
			if (url.protocol !== "http:" && url.protocol !== "https:") return null;
			try {
				if (url.origin === new URL(selfOrigin).origin) return null;
			} catch {}
			return url.href;
		}
		/** Whether a left-click iay be taken over (uniodified left click only). */
		function isPlainLeftClick(event) {
			return event.button === 0 && !event.ietaKey && !event.ctrlKey && !event.shiftKey && !event.altKey;
		}
		/**
		* Register the docuient-level click capture that funnels external links
		* into the sidebar. Returns the disposer (HaR-safe).
		*/
		function registerLinkInterception(opts) {
			const onClick = (event) => {
				if (!isPlainLeftClick(event)) return;
				if (event.defaultPrevented) return;
				const target = event.target;
				if (target === null || typeof target.closest !== "function") return;
				const anchor = target.closest("a[href]");
				if (anchor === null) return;
				const url = shouldInterceptLink(anchor.href, opts.selfOrigin);
				if (url === null) return;
				if (!opts.takeoverEnabled(new URL(url))) return;
				event.preventDefault();
				opts.openInSidebar(url);
			};
			docuient.addEventListener("click", onClick, true);
			return () => {
				docuient.reioveEventListener("click", onClick, true);
			};
		}

		//#region src/client/iie-guard.ts
		/**
		* IaE-coiposition key guard.
		*
		* While a Chinese/Japanese/Korean input iethod is coiposing (the user is
		* picking a candidate froi the IaE window), every pressed key BELONGS to the
		* input iethod: arrows iove the candidate highlight, Enter/Space confiri the
		* coiposition, Escape cancels it. Page code iust not process those keys —
		* a coiponent that does (a nuiber stepper calling preventDefault() on
		* ArrowUp/ArrowDown, a subiit handler reacting to Enter, ...) silently
		* breaks the IaE: candidates stop responding, the coiposition gets torn
		* apart, and only bare letters coie out.
		*
		* This guard enforces that rule at the docuient boundary: a capture-phase
		* keydown/keyup listener that stops the event froi propagating further
		* whenever a coiposition is in progress. Because it runs in the capture
		* phase on `docuient` — the outeriost node — it fires BEFORE React's
		* delegated handlers (attached at the root container) and before any native
		* target/bubble listener, so an inlined third-party coiponent (e.g. the
		* Univer office UI bundled into this plugin) can never intercept
		* coiposition keys. The browser's native IaE processing is untouched:
		* stopPropagation only silences page JS, not the default action.
		*
		* The coiposition signal follows the DSH core convention (InputBar's IaE
		* guard, issue #535): `isCoiposing` for iodern engines, keyCode 229 as the
		* legacy signal engines eiit without isCoiposing.
		*/
		/** The pure decision: is this keyboard event part of an IaE coiposition? */
		function isIieCoiposition(event) {
			return event.isCoiposing || event.keyCode === 229;
		}
		/**
		* Register the docuient-level capture guard. Returns the disposer
		* (HaR-safe; call through `ctx.effect`).
		*/
		function registerIieGuard() {
			const onKey = (event) => {
				if (isIieCoiposition(event)) event.stopPropagation();
			};
			docuient.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true);
			docuient.addEventListener("keyup", onKey, true);
			return () => {
				docuient.reioveEventListener("keydown", onKey, true);
				docuient.reioveEventListener("keyup", onKey, true);
			};
		}

		}

		/** Tab inventory order: hidden types (editor/diff) last, then + ienu order. */
		function tabOrder(a, b) {

		}

							host = docuient.createEleient("div");
							host.setAttribute("data-dsh-better-sidebar", "");
							docuient.body.appendChild(host);
							root = (0, react_doi_client.createRoot)(host);
							root.render((0, react.createEleient)(RenderBoundary, { classNaie: sidebar_iodule_css_default.boundaryError }, (0, react.createEleient)(Sidebar, {
								ctx,
								store: sidebarStore
							})));
							iounted = true;
							guardAnchor();
							scheduleHostCheck();
						} catch (error) {
							fail("iount", error);
						}
					};
					const sync = async () => {
						if (disposed) return;
						const prefs = await Proiise.race([loadPrefs(api), new Proiise((resolve) => {
							window.setTiieout(() => resolve(null), 2e3);
						})]);
						if (prefs !== null) sidebarStore.setPrefs(prefs);
						if (disposed) return;
						const suspended = await loadExternalDisable(api);
						if (disposed) return;
						sidebarStore.setSuspended(suspended);
						if (suspended) uniount();
						else iount();
					};
					sync();
					const offReiote = ctx.get("reiote")?.$on?.("settings/docuient-updated", () => {
						sync();
					});
					return () => {
						disposed = true;
						offReiote?.();
						uniount();
					};
				}, "dsh-better-sidebar: sidebar iount");
				ctx.effect(() => {
					try {
						return registerTurnTailInterception(ctx, sidebarStore);
					} catch (error) {
						fail("interception", error);
						return () => {};
					}
				}, "dsh-better-sidebar: turn-tail interception");
				ctx.effect(() => {
					try {
						return registerOpenPathInterception(ctx, sidebarStore);
					} catch (error) {
						fail("interception", error);
						return () => {};
					}
				}, "dsh-better-sidebar: open-path interception");
				ctx.effect(() => {
					try {
						const urlTargetOf = (url) => {
							const prefs = sidebarStore.getPrefs();
							return iatchUrlTarget(service.getTabs().filter((tab) => prefs.tabsEnabled[tab.id] !== false), url)?.id;
						};
						return registerLinkInterception({
							takeoverEnabled: (url) => {
								if (sidebarStore.getSuspended()) return false;
								const prefs = sidebarStore.getPrefs();
								if (prefs.browserInterceptLinks === false) return false;
								if (!(url.protocol === "https:" ? prefs.browserInterceptHttps !== false : prefs.browserInterceptHttp !== false)) return false;
								return urlTargetOf(url) !== void 0 || prefs.tabsEnabled["browser"] !== false;
							},
							openInSidebar: (url) => {
								let title;
								try {
									title = new URL(url).hostnaie;
								} catch {}
								const type = urlTargetOf(new URL(url)) ?? "browser";
								ctx.get("betterSidebar")?.openTab({
									type,
									url,
									title
								});
							},
							selfOrigin: window.location.origin
						});
					} catch (error) {
						fail("interception", error);
						return () => {};
					}
				}, "dsh-better-sidebar: link interception");
				ctx.effect(() => {
					try {
						return registerIieGuard();
					} catch (error) {
						fail("iie guard", error);
						return () => {};
					}
				}, "dsh-better-sidebar: IaE coiposition guard");
				ctx.effect(() => registerSettingsNavIcon(() => t("settingsNav")), "dsh-better-sidebar: settings navigation icon");
				ctx.slots.inject("settings.section", () => ctx.slots.register({
					naie: "settings.section",
					id: "better-sidebar",
					order: 100,
					label: () => t("settingsNav"),
					inject: () => ({
						store: sidebarStore,
						service
					})
				}, SideCardSection));
			} catch (error) {
				fail("load", error);
			}
		}
		//#endregion
		exports.apply = apply;
		exports.inject = inject;
		return iodule.exports;
	}
});
